clue.text: Fascinating time legally recognised

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time, as in a cold spell
a binding agreement is one the law will enforce

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled that a moment has finally been given official legal standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fascinating time' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after the first word and the time is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spellbinding holds attention completely, as if casting an enchantment, which is a synonym for captivating.

clue.text: Planted whole, a fruit

blocks.note: to be planted somewhere is to have sat down firmly there
a sum is a whole amount, a total
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone planting an entire tree, perhaps an orange tree, to grow fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planted whole' suggests a gardener putting in an entire tree, but planted means seated, as in 'planted himself on the sofa'.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small loose-skinned citrus variety, a kind of mandarin orange, so it is an example.

clue.text: Stick raised, time to perform

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a cane is a walking stick
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A conductor lifts the baton: time for the orchestra to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The raised stick looks like a conductor's baton, but it is a cane to be turned upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a play or scene is to act it out on stage, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Red meat American company packed with last of flour

indicators.note: the last of something is its final element, so only the closing letter is wanted
a case packed with goods has them stuffed inside it, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: lamb is the meat of a young sheep
US is the standard abbreviation for American
Co is the abbreviation for company
the final letter of the word flour

explanation.surface: A shopping list of red meat from an American firm, packed in with flour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red meat' reads as one phrase, but Red alone is the definition, meaning red wine; the single letter slips into the case just after the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling Italian wine, usually red, and 'red' on its own is common shorthand for red wine.

clue.text: Keen on a little Chopin, toddler

indicators.note: a little of something is only a portion of it, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the last two letters of the composer's name plus the first two of the next word

explanation.surface: A small child who already loves hearing a bit of Chopin.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle chopIN TOddler, ignoring the comma between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is informal for being enthusiastic about it, a colloquial synonym for liking.

clue.text: Custard spattered over back of dirtiest rubbish truck

indicators.note: something spattered is splashed about, so its letters are scattered into a new order
the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of dirtiest

explanation.surface: Custard splashed all over the grimy rear of a bin lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: A dustcart is the British term for a refuse collection lorry, the vehicle that empties household bins.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustcart is the vehicle councils send round to collect household refuse, a British word for a garbage truck.

clue.text: Fibre in sauce?

blocks.note: first meaning: a bundle of fibres carrying signals through the body
second meaning: sauce is cheek or impudence

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about dietary fibre in a sauce; in fact sauce is British slang for cheeky boldness.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve is a fibre conducting impulses in the body, and having the nerve means showing cheek or audacity.

clue.text: Repeatedly on and off relationship hugging tree!

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap the arms around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a fling is a short casual affair
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: An on-off romance, with a couple of tree-huggers at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On and off relationship' wants to be a single phrase, but the definition ends at 'off' and the relationship is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A light that is flashing turns on and off in quick succession, so the description fits exactly.

clue.text: Union member has kept line in check

indicators.note: what someone has kept is held within their possession, so one piece stays inside another

blocks.note: a bride is one partner in the union of marriage
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A trade unionist keeping the workforce in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union member' suggests a trade union; here the union is a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to restrain or curb, from the headgear that controls a horse, a synonym for keeping in check.

clue.text: See one mat and another mat turned on the same side

indicators.note: something turned is twisted round, so these letters are spun into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
a single mat, taken as written
a second mat, taken as written

explanation.surface: Two rugs flipped over so they lie the same way up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'same side' suggests the upper face of a rug; it is the side players are on.
explanation.definitionFit: Teammates are players belonging to one squad, so they are all on the same side in a game.

clue.text: Head measurer

blocks.note: first meaning: the head of a state, a sovereign
second meaning: a straight strip used to measure length

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests something that measures heads, like a hatter's tape; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who governs is the head of a country, and a graduated straightedge measures lengths in school.

clue.text: Improvement when put off vessel

indicators.note: food that is off has gone bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: Things get better once someone is dropped off a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off vessel' reads like being put ashore, and vessel suggests a boat; it is a container for liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is a rise in fortunes or figures, as in an economic upturn, so it means a turn for the better.

clue.text: A cold, cold ebbing river into which ship entered

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back the way it came, so these letters run backwards
something goes into the item just named, so one piece sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
the same abbreviation again
the Dee is a river in Britain
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship sailing into a freezing river as the tide goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee runs through Wales and England; a steamship goes inside it once it has been flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To access a place or a computer file is to gain entry to it, so accessed means went in.

clue.text: Bacon, say, as rasher that is sizzling there, first of all

indicators.note: the first of all the words means the opening letter of each one in turn

blocks.clueFragment: as rasher that is sizzling there
blocks.note: the initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: Bacon described in the pan as a rasher sizzling away.
explanation.walkthrough: The breakfast picture points at streaky bacon, but Bacon is Francis Bacon, the twentieth-century painter known for distorted figures; a rasher is a slice of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was a celebrated British painter, so he is one example of a painter or creative practitioner.

clue.text: Complete, but unrefined

blocks.note: tho is an informal spelling of though, which can mean but
something rough is crude and unpolished

explanation.surface: A finished job that is nonetheless crude.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma and 'but' make it look like two contrasting descriptions; the conjunction is itself a piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough means absolute or utter, as in a thorough nuisance, which matches complete used as an intensifier.

clue.text: Proceed to cut cost for convention

indicators.note: a blade that cuts goes into the material, so one piece is driven inside another

blocks.note: to act is to proceed or take action
a price is what something costs

explanation.surface: An instruction to go ahead and slash the budget for a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convention' suggests a conference that needs cost-cutting; it means an established custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice is a customary way of doing things, such as standard business practice, matching a convention or usage.

clue.text: A canister destroyed using axes?

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are rebuilt in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tin smashed apart with hatchets.
explanation.walkthrough: Axes here are the plural of axis, not axe; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartesian coordinates, named after Descartes, locate points by measuring distances along perpendicular reference lines on a graph.

clue.text: Very long scar on a shortened strip of leather

indicators.note: making something shorter trims its end, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: to mar is to scar or disfigure
taken as written
a thong is a narrow strip of leather

explanation.surface: A long scar left by a lash from a leather strap.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' means the first piece sits above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathon is used as an adjective for something lasting an exhaustingly long time, as in a marathon meeting.

clue.text: Suggestion also formulated by rugby player

indicators.note: to formulate is to devise or compose, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby player has also put forward an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' tells you the rugby player stands beside the rearranged letters, here in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a plan or idea put forward for consideration, a direct synonym for a suggestion.

clue.text: Photograph animal that climbs, little monkey

indicators.note: something climbing goes upward, and in a down entry that reads the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: pic is short for picture
the elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a small monkey scampering up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The monkey looks like a real animal, but 'little monkey' is an affectionate name for a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickle is a British affectionate term for a naughty child, just as a little monkey is a playful scamp.

clue.text: Short song about US soldier, very sad

indicators.note: a short version has had its end trimmed, so the last letter goes
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a track is a song on an album
GI is the standard term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A brief ballad about an American soldier that is deeply moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short song' suggests a ditty, but it means a track with its tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something causing great sorrow or distress, which matches deeply sad.

clue.text: Wonderful thing, something for Christmas?

blocks.note: first meaning: British informal for an excellent example of something
second meaning: a paper tube pulled apart with a bang at Christmas dinner

explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a British festive novelty: a wrapped tube two people pull until it snaps, releasing a paper hat and a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a cracker is British slang for praising it highly, and the festive novelty is a holiday staple.

clue.text: European raincoat in a storm?

indicators.note: things caught in a storm are tossed about, so these letters are blown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A continental mackintosh, perhaps one worn during bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European raincoat' reads as a description of the coat, but European is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croatian is a native of Croatia, a country in south-eastern Europe, so is one example.

clue.text: Little piggies perhaps run into you

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: thee is the old form of you
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Small pigs charging straight at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the nursery tale of the Three Little Pigs; 'perhaps' warns that it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy tale features three little pigs, so the number counts them, defined loosely by example.

clue.text: Old country in America is republican, though left-leaning?

indicators.note: something in a phrase is contained within it, so the letters lie inside the words that follow
leaning to the left points westward, which in an across entry means reading right to left

blocks.note: the last letter of the country, the whole of the little verb and the start of the party label

explanation.surface: A US Republican who is somehow politically on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-leaning' looks political, an oxymoron beside republican, but it tells you to read the concealed letters backwards: americA IS REPublican.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the former name of Iran, used until 1935, so it is a country under an older name.

clue.text: A sinful hanger-on?

blocks.note: surface reading: a disreputable parasite clinging to someone
setter's reading: one of the seven deadly sins that is also a slow mammal hanging from branches

explanation.walkthrough: The answer names both the deadly sin of idleness and the tree-dwelling animal that spends its life hanging upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness is one of the seven deadly sins, and the same word names a South American mammal that dangles from trees.

clue.text: Twenty per cent off bird, bargain!

indicators.note: a fifth taken away from a five-letter word removes exactly one letter

blocks.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: A shop sign announcing a discounted bird at a bargain price.
explanation.walkthrough: The discount sounds like a sale price, but it is one letter of five removed from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is British informal for something sold cheaply, an unexpectedly good buy.

clue.text: Drink that's glorious, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

blocks.note: regal means splendid and kingly

explanation.surface: Thinking back, the beer really was magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as 'thinking it over', but it means mirror-image letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light fizzy beer, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Artistic design, how a drink developed

indicators.note: something developed has evolved into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An art piece tracing the history of a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a story about how a drink came to be; 'developed' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Handiwork is something made skilfully by hand, so a crafted or creative piece of work fits.

clue.text: Girl wanting dog, reportedly – one unlikely to buy it?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: Penny is a girl's name
a pinscher is a breed of dog, as in Dobermann pinscher

explanation.surface: A girl begs for a puppy, but someone tight with money won't pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl wants the dog, but 'it' in the definition is the dog too: a miser would refuse to buy it.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny-pincher is a miser who avoids spending, so such a stingy person is unlikely to purchase anything.
